name: Wood-type poster
summary: A bill set in large letters cut from end-grain wood, printed on a hand or a job press in one or two flat inks. Darius Wells made the type cheap in 1828; the auction, the circus and the theatre filled walls with stacked lines of fat faces and slabs.

philosophy.core_thesis: A poster is a stack of words, and each line takes the largest and boldest type that fits the width.
design_principles: Centre each line and set it in the largest type that fills the measure.
Change the face, the width and the size from line to line; three to six faces on one sheet are normal.
Put the key word (the act, the date, the price) in the largest line, often in a second ink.
Print flat ink with no tone: black for the text and one red or blue for the accent.
Use rules, stars and a stock wood or metal cut as the only images.
Keep the tight vertical rhythm of the chase: little space between the lines.
anti_patterns: A photograph or a tone in the image
One face at one size for all lines
Thin, light type or a script face

process.matrix: Letters routed from end-grain maple with a pantograph, locked in a chase with metal rules and cuts.
process.press: A hand press or a platen job press; large sheets on a cylinder press.
process.image_making: A jobbing printer sets the type by eye from the cases in stock, proofs and prints.
process.edition: Hundreds of copies, the run for one event, then the forme is broken up.

inks.strategy: Black for the body and one bright second ink, each from its own forme or a split fountain.

colours.name: Poster red
colours.role: the key words and the rules

screening.rule: Print flat, full ink; the only tone is the grain of the worn wood.

registration.rule: The second ink can shift about 1 mm; a red line can sit a little above or below its place.

substrate.stock: A cheap, thin poster or news stock, often tinted buff, yellow or pink.
substrate.finish: Uncoated, soft, with a visible fibre.

surface.impression: A light bite and a dark rim of ink round each letter.
surface.sheen: Matt, with some gloss in heavy solids.
surface.texture: Solid letters with worn edges, specks of missing ink and the grain of the wood in large letters.

marks: second ink a little off register

emotion.target_response: Loud, honest announcement: the viewer reads it from across the street and feels a show is in town.

avoid_when: The message needs an image, a photograph or long text.
The brand must look quiet or refined.

modifiers.how: Add a full-colour drawn picture in crayon lithography and keep the type at the top and the bottom.
Change the mixed display faces for one text face, set in black and red on handmade paper.

sources.title: Rob Roy Kelly, American Wood Type 1828–1900 (Van Nostrand Reinhold, 1969)
